query_log.query: pose occlusion uncertainty conformal human motion
query_log.result_summary: Located multimodal and uncertainty-aware pose or motion work, including MotionMap, CHAMP, CUPS, and conformal motion-prediction records; these produce pose or motion hypotheses/distributions rather than repetition-count sets.

query_log.query: repetition counting pose missing joints uncertainty
query_log.result_summary: Located skeleton-based repetition segmentation/counting and SSTRAC's defective-skeleton reconstruction and occlusion evaluation. The checked sources emphasize repair or point prediction, not calibrated task-level count intervals.

query_log.query: set-valued event count missing data uncertainty
query_log.result_summary: The raw arXiv query was low precision. Targeted primary-source follow-up located conformal pose and motion forecasting, but no mechanism-matched direct RAC source in the checked set. This is a search result, not an absence proof.

query_log.query: multi object tracking tracklet fragmentation re-entry repair
channels: CVF, NeurIPS, publisher, and official-code search
query_log.result_summary: Located GTA, STAR, TrackTrack, Split and Connect, probabilistic tracklet inpainting, GTATrack, and SRITrack. Tracklet reconnection, re-entry handling, and long-occlusion repair are crowded adjacent mechanisms.

query_log.query: repetition counting count density temporal additivity
query_log.result_summary: Located direct density/response RAC work including RepNet, TransRAC, MultiCounter, Motion Feature Learning, Rethinking TSSM, PAMS, and TWCRAC. Density integration and temporal consistency are established; explicit supplied-track fragment-boundary count-mass composition was not found in the checked accessible text.

query_log.query: track fragment endpoint consistency count conservation
query_log.result_summary: The literal query was low precision. Targeted follow-up found generic tracklet splitting/linking, gap inpainting, and people-flow conservation, but no checked source that combines these as a repetition-count boundary transport law. This is unresolved rather than novelty clearance.

papers.title: Counting Out Time: Class Agnostic Video Repetition Counting in the Wild
papers.authors_display: Debidatta Dwibedi, Yusuf Aytar, Jonathan Tompson, Pierre Sermanet, Andrew Zisserman
papers.core_contribution: RepNet uses temporal self-similarity, synthetic repetitions, and per-frame period and periodicity predictions for class-agnostic point counting.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Foundational direct boundary for synthetic repetition and response integration; it does not report calibrated count sets or a supplied-track fragment-boundary transport law.

papers.title: TransRAC: Encoding Multi-scale Temporal Correlation with Transformers for Repetitive Action Counting
papers.authors_display: Huazhang Hu, Sixun Dong, Yiqun Zhao, Dongze Lian, Zhengxin Li, Shenghua Gao
papers.core_contribution: Multi-scale temporal correlation and density-map regression establish a direct count-density baseline.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Global density integration is established; explicit correction or abstention at supplied-track fragment joins is not disclosed in the checked paper.

papers.title: Repetitive Activity Counting by Sight and Sound
papers.authors_display: Yunhua Zhang, Ling Shao, Cees G. M. Snoek
papers.core_contribution: Audiovisual fusion and reliability estimation improve point counting under poor visual conditions including occlusion.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: RAC reliability under occlusion is occupied, but the checked method switches or fuses modalities rather than producing calibrated count intervals or abstention guarantees.

papers.title: MultiCounter: Multiple Action Agnostic Repetition Counting in Untrimmed Videos
papers.authors_display: Yin Tang, Wei Luo, Jinrui Zhang, Wei Huang, Ruihai Jing, Deyu Zhang
papers.core_contribution: Joint multi-instance localization, tracking, period, and periodicity heads support per-instance count accumulation in untrimmed video.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: It is the closest direct identity-continuity boundary. Checked text treats severe occlusion or absence through an empty location state and sums per-frame periodic response, but does not expose calibrated count intervals or post-hoc count-mass transport across externally supplied fragments.

papers.title: Repetitive Action Counting With Motion Feature Learning
papers.authors_display: Xinjie Li, Huijuan Xu
papers.core_contribution: A motion branch, flow-guided attention, temporal self-similarity reconstruction, and density-map counting address background changes.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Motion representation and TSSM reconstruction are occupied; fragment-specific composition and boundary uncertainty are not the stated contribution.

papers.title: Rethinking Temporal Self-Similarity for Repetitive Action Counting
papers.authors_display: Yanan Luo, Jinhui Yi, Yazan Abu Farha, Moritz Wolter, Juergen Gall
papers.core_contribution: Full-resolution embeddings, action-start probabilities, and a reference-TSM consistency loss replace direct TSM-to-count prediction.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Temporal response consistency and start-response integration are occupied; explicit count-mass conservation over supplied fragment joins is not disclosed.

papers.title: SSTRAC: Skeleton-Based Dual-Stream Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Repetitive Action Counting in Videos
papers.authors_display: Jungjun Lim, Donghoon Kang, Kanghyun Ryu, Je Hyeong Hong
papers.core_contribution: Defective skeletons are reconstructed before a dual-stream spatiotemporal transformer predicts a repetition density map; experiments include occlusion robustness.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Pose repair and skeleton occlusion robustness are directly occupied. The checked source is a repair-plus-point-count method, not task-level set-valued counting.

papers.title: MultiCounter+: Toward Efficient and Robust Multi-Instance Repetitive Action Counting
papers.authors_display: Yin Tang, Deyu Zhang, Wei Luo, Jinrui Zhang, Wei Huang, Ruihai Jing, Yaoxue Zhang
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
papers.core_contribution: Publisher metadata describes efficient robust multi-instance counting with mixed spatiotemporal interaction, spatial-temporal consistency, long-short period awareness, and synthetic pretraining.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: This is a required mechanism-matched boundary for robust MRAC and identity consistency. Full text was not retrieved, so fragmentation/re-entry and uncertainty details remain unresolved.

papers.title: Count What Repeats: Period-Adaptive Multi-Scale Consistency for Self-Supervised Repetitive Action Counting
papers.authors_display: Shizhao Gao, Jun Li, Qiming Li
papers.core_contribution: Period-adaptive multi-scale temporal cycle consistency supports self-supervised representation learning, while multi-expert peak consensus produces the final count.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Local/multi-scale cycle consistency and dynamic peak aggregation are occupied. The checked method does not state calibrated count sets or supplied-track fragment-boundary count transport.

papers.title: TWCRAC: Leveraging Temporal Cycle Consistency and Dynamic Thresholding for Robust Repetitive Action Counting
papers.authors_display: Jun Li, Shizhao Gao, Tianwen Hu, Yinhui Xie, Zhonghua Liu, Qiming Li
papers.core_contribution: The accessible abstract describes a time-window-cycle construction, intra-video temporal cycle consistency, and local-statistics dynamic thresholds for nonstationary repetition.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Time-window/crop consistency and dynamic thresholds cannot be claimed. Full-text access is required to resolve whether any boundary or uncertainty mechanism is closer than the abstract indicates.

papers.title: DeepPhase: Periodic Autoencoders for Learning Motion Phase Manifolds
papers.authors_display: Sebastian Starke, Ian Mason, Taku Komura
papers.core_contribution: Periodic autoencoders learn multi-channel motion phase manifolds without phase labels.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Learned phase and motion-manifold components are occupied and are not count-uncertainty or fragment-transport contributions.

papers.title: CHAMP: Conformalized 3D Human Multi-Hypothesis Pose Estimators
papers.authors_display: Harry Zhang, Luca Carlone
papers.core_contribution: A learned conformity score selects sets of 3D pose hypotheses from 2D keypoints for downstream aggregation.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Generic conformal pose-set construction is occupied; a residual would need to be specifically about propagating pose ambiguity through a repetition-count functional and showing useful count-set behavior.

papers.title: CUPS: Improving Human Pose-Shape Estimators with Conformalized Deep Uncertainty
papers.authors_display: Harry Zhang, Luca Carlone
papers.core_contribution: Multiple pose-shape hypotheses and conformalized deep uncertainty support calibrated sequence estimation, including nonexchangeability analysis.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Pose/shape uncertainty calibration is strongly occupied; the checked paper does not target repetition counts.

papers.title: Toward Reliable Human Pose Forecasting With Uncertainty
papers.authors_display: Saeed Saadatnejad et al.
papers.core_contribution: Pose forecasting models aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty using learned motion priors and clustered forecasts.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Uncertain future-pose prediction is occupied but is not calibrated repetition-count set prediction.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware calibrated 3D human motion forecasting with latent conformal prediction
papers.authors_display: Yue Ma, Frederick W. B. Li, Xiaohui Liang
papers.core_contribution: Latent conformal prediction calibrates probabilistic 3D human-motion forecasts.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Task-adjacent calibrated motion uncertainty is occupied. The final full text was not fully inspected, and no repetition-count output is identified in the accessible record.

papers.title: MotionMap: Representing Multimodality in Human Pose Forecasting
papers.authors_display: Reyhaneh Hosseininejad, Megh Shukla, Saeed Saadatnejad, Mathieu Salzmann, Alexandre Alahi
papers.core_contribution: A heatmap representation expresses a variable number of plausible future-motion modes and per-mode confidence.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Multimodal pose confidence is occupied; it is not a coverage-guaranteed count interval.

papers.title: Vision-Based Safe Human-Robot Collaboration with Uncertainty Guarantees
papers.authors_display: Jakob Thumm, Marian Frei, Tianle Ni, Matthias Althoff, Marco Pavone
papers.core_contribution: Recent conformal sets are used around vision-based pose or motion estimates to support safety guarantees in human-robot collaboration.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: This recent-window source reinforces that conformal pose-to-downstream propagation is active adjacent territory, but the downstream target is safety rather than repetition count.

papers.title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
papers.authors_display: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Stephen Bates
papers.core_contribution: Foundational distribution-free prediction-set framework and coverage concepts.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Generic conformal methodology cannot be a candidate contribution. Any count-set claim must specify exchangeability or shift assumptions, task-level coverage, width, and non-vacuity.

papers.title: GTA: Global Tracklet Association for Multi-Object Tracking in Sports
papers.authors_display: Jiacheng Sun, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Cheng-Yen Yang, Zhongyu Jiang, Jenq-Neng Hwang
papers.core_contribution: Appearance-based global tracklet association splits mixed-identity tracklets and reconnects same-identity tracklets, including exit/re-entry in sports.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Generic fragment repair and re-entry linking are occupied. A supplied-track RAC study must not claim tracking or re-identification novelty.

papers.title: STAR: Spatial-Temporal Tracklet Matching for Multi-Object Tracking
papers.authors_display: Xuewei Bai, Yongcai Wang, Deying Li, Haodi Ping, Chunxu Li

papers.boundary_to_pivots: Long-term tracklet matching is occupied and narrows the candidate to a count-functional composition question, not identity association.

papers.title: Focusing on Tracks for Online Multi-Object Tracking
papers.authors_display: Kyujin Shim et al.
papers.core_contribution: Track-aware initialization and association emphasize the track perspective and low-confidence detections in online MOT.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Track continuity and occlusion-aware association are adjacent occupied territory, without a repetition-count composition law.

papers.title: Visual multi-object tracking with re-identification and occlusion handling using labeled random finite sets
papers.authors_display: Linh Van Ma et al.
papers.core_contribution: A labeled-random-finite-set formulation addresses disappearance, reappearance, re-identification, and occlusion.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Probabilistic re-entry and identity continuity are occupied adjacent mechanisms; no count-density transport is identified in the accessible record.

papers.title: GTATrack: Winner Solution to SoccerTrack 2025 with Deep-EIoU and Global Tracklet Association
papers.authors_display: Rong-Lin Jian et al.
papers.core_contribution: Sports MOT combines association improvements with global tracklet association.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: A current 2026 example of tracklet repair in the relevant sports setting; it reinforces that generic re-linking is not a count-method contribution. Its initial arXiv date precedes the strict recent-six-month cutoff.

papers.authors_display: Yu Yung Kao, Po Yung Chou, Cheng Hung Lin

papers.boundary_to_pivots: Recent re-entry handling is occupied adjacent territory; full text was not obtained and count composition is not described in the accessible record.

papers.title: GOT-JEPA: Generic Object Tracking with Model Adaptation and Occlusion Handling using Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
papers.authors_display: Shih-Fang Chen et al.
papers.core_contribution: Recent generic single-object tracking uses adaptation and explicit occlusion handling.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: This is a recent-window occlusion-handling signal, not multi-instance re-entry or repetition-count transport.

papers.authors_display: Gaoang Wang, Yizhou Wang, Renshu Gu, Weijie Hu, Jenq-Neng Hwang

papers.boundary_to_pivots: The split/reconnect template is established and is a close objection to any generic endpoint-pairing claim.

papers.core_contribution: A stochastic autoregressive motion model scores tracklet proposals and inpaints gaps caused by long occlusion.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Gap inference and tracklet repair are established; a candidate must separate count-mass correction from trajectory inpainting.

papers.title: Estimating People Flows to Better Count Them in Crowded Scenes
papers.authors_display: Weizhe Liu, Mathieu Salzmann, Pascal Fua
papers.core_contribution: People counting is constrained through inter-frame flow and conservation of population mass.
papers.boundary_to_pivots: Conservation-based counting is established in an adjacent domain. It concerns objects moving across frames, not repetition events or count response across identity fragments.

theme_map.theme: Pose repair and occlusion-robust point counting
theme_map.occupied_ground: Repairing defective skeletons, fusing a reliable modality, and robust point prediction under occlusion.
theme_map.open_landscape_question: Whether pose missingness can be propagated into a useful task-level repetition-count set without pretending self-containment is true-count coverage.

theme_map.theme: Pose and motion hypothesis sets and uncertainty calibration
theme_map.occupied_ground: Multi-hypothesis pose or motion prediction, learned uncertainty, conformal prediction sets, and distribution-free coverage concepts.
theme_map.open_landscape_question: Whether the count functional and non-vacuity evaluation create a defensible task-specific residual beyond applying generic conformal or set-prediction machinery.

theme_map.theme: Track fragmentation, re-entry, association, and gap repair
theme_map.occupied_ground: Tracklet splitting, linking, graph matching, re-entry identity enhancement, probabilistic gap inpainting, and robust association.
theme_map.open_landscape_question: Whether a count-functional correction across already supplied fragments remains separable from generic tracking or interpolation.

theme_map.theme: Count density, response integration, additivity, and temporal consistency
theme_map.occupied_ground: Density integration, action-start or periodic response accumulation, TSSM reconstruction, local or multi-scale cycle consistency, and conservation-based counting in adjacent domains.
theme_map.open_landscape_question: Whether an explicit boundary term yields a testable composition law for repetition-count response across fragments, rather than merely preserving a biased base response.

actual_gaps.statement: Across the checked direct RAC sources, occlusion is handled through repair, modality reliability, robustness, or point prediction; across the checked pose-UQ sources, uncertainty is attached to pose or future motion. No checked accessible primary source directly propagates missing-pose uncertainty to a calibrated, non-vacuous repetition-count interval.
actual_gaps.qualification: This does not confirm novelty. The search can have missed terminology, inaccessible text, or task-level uncertainty work outside the indexed set.

actual_gaps.statement: The candidate's proposed containment of its own unmasked estimate is a deterministic self-consistency property, not empirical coverage of the true repetition count.
actual_gaps.qualification: Any later claim would need a declared target, exchangeability or shift assumptions, coverage evaluation against labels after freezing, interval width, abstention rate, and non-vacuity controls.

actual_gaps.statement: The checked tracking literature strongly covers fragment splitting, re-linking, re-entry, and gap inpainting, while direct RAC covers response integration and temporal consistency. No checked accessible source explicitly learns an additive repetition-count-mass composition law with a boundary correction across supplied identity fragments and abstention when the join is unidentifiable.
actual_gaps.qualification: This does not confirm novelty; generic tracklet repair plus density conservation may absorb the idea after full-text adjudication.

actual_gaps.statement: A boundary law trained only to reproduce an intact frozen response can conserve the base method's bias and may become unidentifiable across long gaps or tempo changes.
actual_gaps.qualification: The literature landscape supports treating negative or abstaining outcomes as informative, but authorizes no experiment here.

actual_gaps.statement: In a supplied-track protocol, the residual cannot be framed as tracking, re-identification, generic endpoint matching, temporal consistency, or density integration.
actual_gaps.qualification: A later predicted-track study would separately require tracking metrics and is outside the current landscape.

failure_boundary.rule: Do not tune, retry, reinterpret, or resurrect WARP-PHASE, its selector, fixture population, harmonic rules, or server route.
failure_boundary.effect_on_landscape: No paper was used to reopen the WARP-PHASE route, and neither selected direction is treated as a phase-integral repair.

conclusion.direction_A: The checked landscape leaves a narrowly stated and unconfirmed task-level question around non-vacuous count intervals under pose missingness, while generic pose repair, uncertainty, and conformal sets are clearly occupied.
conclusion.direction_B: The checked landscape leaves a narrowly stated and unconfirmed count-functional composition question, while fragment repair, re-entry, identity continuity, density integration, and temporal consistency are clearly occupied.
conclusion.next_stage_if_authorized_elsewhere: Primary-source full-text adjudication of MultiCounter+, TWCRAC, SRITrack, and mechanism-matched count-UQ/event-count literature would be required before any novelty verdict.
conclusion.authorization: No implementation, training, result production, novelty claim, or paper claim is authorized by this landscape.
